text:
Morgan Geekie spent the first few weeks of the season answering questions about where the goals went. Then he scored in three straight games and the headlines flipped from "slow start" to "bounces back." Our numbers never really moved. He has 4 goals and 13 points in 17 games on 5.02 expected goals of his own (expected goals measure the quality of a player's chances), so if anything he is still a goal light.

The bigger change from last year is how he gets them. Six of his 13 points have come on the power play, where his one-timer from the right circle is a real weapon: his hardest recorded shot sits in the 99th percentile of the league. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him on the end of a lot of royal-road passes, the cross-slot feeds that beat goalies far more often than a shooter's own play.

The 39 goals of last season are not walking through the door again. Our range has him around 19 to 33 this year. What to watch: Boston's chances at 5v5 with him on the ice are only about even, so the power play is carrying his line.
headline: Geekie's goals came back, as they were always going to
